{"self_assessment": "Impact: I held the pad and sketched the fish the table built, with a clear outline, a forked tail, top and bottom edges leaving START together, and an eye label. The telltale parts were all drawn, which is what a judge needs. I can't say yet whether the judge recognised it, because I haven't seen the result, and I don't want to claim a win I haven't seen. The main risk was Tom's bottom edge. At 9:30 it was still three dominoes short of the fork and he hadn't called it in, so the tail may depend on that joint.

Execution: I laid my bottom tail tip from the fork, confirmed the notch belonged to strokes three and four, and kept the stroke numbers clear for everyone. My weak spot was that I never ran a close inspect of the whole chain before the push. I had flagged the nose joint where strokes one and two meet as risky in my own notes, but I didn't check it myself, and I didn't get the final check on the fork done.

Collaboration: I stayed off Tom's bottom join as he asked and left the start domino to Leo, who had traced stroke one. I offered Tom a second pair of hands at 8:30, he declined, and I respected that. I don't know what Leo said quietly to Tom, so I can't speak to it.

Leadership: I set the fish plan, kept stroke ownership clear, and kept the table steady during the wait. But I didn't push for an early joint check while there was still time to fix the fork. Next time I'll call for that check sooner and take responsibility for the riskiest joints, rather than waiting to be asked."}
